title: allow
summary: Records a dl:ok review of one finding, so it stops being reported without being fixed
intro: Read this when a lint finding is a deliberate, reviewed exception that you do not intend to fix. allow records a dl:ok review for that one finding (identified by file, line and rule) so it stops being reported; without --apply it is a dry run.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint allow <file> --fix-line <L> --fix-rule <id> [--apply] [--rules-dir <dir>] [--config <file>] [--profile <name>] [--enable id,...] [--disable id,...] [--stand-in-for <realpath>] (record a dl:ok review of ONE finding; dry-run without --apply; the lint options decide which findings the line has)
help: drag-lint allow <file>       --fix-line <L> --fix-rule <id> [--apply] [--rules-dir <dir>] [--config <file>] [--profile <name>] [--enable id,...] [--disable id,...] [--stand-in-for <realpath>]   (record a dl:ok review of ONE finding; dry-run without --apply; the lint options decide which findings the line has)

questions.ask: How do I mark one lint finding as a deliberate, reviewed exception?
Can I preview the dl:ok review before it is written?
